videos.title: What if ALL of India lived in Mumbai? 🤯
videos.description:
What if all 1.4 billion Indians lived in Mumbai? It would be over 100 times more crowded than it is today.

Mumbai city covers only about 600 square kilometres and is already one of the most crowded cities on Earth. In this short we look at what would happen to homes, local trains, water supply and the city limits if the whole country moved in.

📌 Quick facts
• Mumbai city: about 603 square kilometres (BMC)
• India: about 1.4 billion people
• That works out to roughly 2.3 million people per square kilometre, against about 20,000 in Mumbai today
Figures are approximate and rounded.

videos.title: What if CHAI disappeared from India? ☕
videos.description:
What if chai vanished from India overnight? India drinks most of the tea it grows, and every morning hundreds of millions of cups are poured.

Roadside chai sellers outside offices, bus stands and railway stations would lose their only income. Tea estates in Assam, Darjeeling and the Nilgiris, and the more than a million workers who depend on them, would be hit next. And the tapri conversation, the office break and the long train wait would go quiet.

📌 Quick facts
• India drinks most of the tea it grows
• More than a million workers depend on tea estates in Assam, Darjeeling and the Nilgiris
• A century ago most Indians did not drink tea every day; it became the national drink in a few generations
Figures are approximate and rounded.

videos.title: What if Delhi's air became clean overnight? 🌤️
videos.description:
What if Delhi's air was perfectly clean tomorrow? Here is how life in the city would change.

Every winter Delhi's air quality often goes many times above the safe limit. With clean air there would be fewer asthma cases, children playing outside, schools staying open in November, fewer smog delays, and a clear view of the sky and the Red Fort.

📌 Quick facts
• Delhi winter air often reaches the CPCB "severe" band (AQI above 400)
• The CPCB "good" band is an AQI of 0 to 50
• Comparing smog to smoking cigarettes is common but approximate
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

videos.title: What if every FARMER in India stopped for a WEEK? 🌾
videos.description:
What if every farmer in India stopped working for a week? Nearly half of India’s workforce is in farming, and they grow the food for about 1.4 billion people.

Grain stocks in government godowns would last a while. The fresh things would go first: milk, vegetables and fruit do not wait. By day two the mandis would be empty and city prices would jump, and crops left unwatered or unharvested would start to spoil.

📌 Quick facts
• Nearly half of India’s workforce works in farming
• In June 2018 farmers in several states held a ten-day protest and some cities felt shortages of milk and vegetables
• A nationwide stoppage would be far bigger
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

💬 Have you ever thought about who grows your food? Tell us in the comments.

videos.title: अगर भारत का हर राज्य एक अलग देश होता? 🇮🇳
videos.description:
अगर भारत का हर राज्य एक अलग देश होता, तो क्या होता?

भारत में 28 राज्य हैं। अकेला उत्तर प्रदेश आबादी में रूस और जापान, दोनों से बड़ा है, जबकि सिक्किम में सिर्फ़ लगभग 6 लाख लोग रहते हैं। इस शॉर्ट में देखिए कि अगर हर राज्य अपना देश बन जाए, तो नक्शा, भाषाएँ और सरहदें कैसे बदल जातीं।

📌 मुख्य तथ्य
• भारत में 28 राज्य और 8 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश हैं
• उत्तर प्रदेश: लगभग 19.98 करोड़ लोग (जनगणना 2011), यानी रूस (लगभग 14.4 करोड़) और जापान (लगभग 12.4 करोड़) से ज़्यादा
• महाराष्ट्र: लगभग 11.2 करोड़ लोग (जनगणना 2011)
• सिक्किम: 6,10,577 लोग (जनगणना 2011), सबसे कम आबादी वाला राज्य
• संविधान की आठवीं अनुसूची में 22 भाषाएँ दर्ज हैं
राज्यों के आँकड़े जनगणना 2011 के हैं; दूसरे देशों के आँकड़े अनुमानित हैं।

🎬 ऐसे और "अगर ऐसा होता तो?" वीडियो के लिए फ़ॉलो करें।

💬 आपके हिसाब से कौन सा राज्य सबसे ताक़तवर देश बनता? कमेंट में बताइए।

videos.title: What if every Indian state was its own country? 🇮🇳
videos.description:
What if every Indian state was its own country? India would split into 28 nations, and one state would suddenly be bigger than Brazil.

In 1947 over 500 princely states could have said no to India, and Travancore (today's Kerala) actually declared itself independent for about six weeks. So we flip it: what if every state said no? Uttar Pradesh would outgrow Brazil, Maharashtra would keep Mumbai, your office in Gurugram would be in a different country, and the IPL would become a World Cup.

📌 Quick facts
• India has 28 states and 8 union territories
• At independence in 1947 there were over 500 princely states (565 is the usual count)
• Travancore (mostly today's Kerala) announced it would stay independent and joined India about six weeks later
• Uttar Pradesh: about 241 million people (2024 estimate); Brazil: about 212 million (UN World Population Prospects 2024)
• Maharashtra holds Mumbai, India's financial capital; Gurugram is in Haryana, next to Delhi
• The map uses the Survey of India outline
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

💬 Which state would be the strongest country? Tell us in the comments.

videos.title: What if every vehicle in India went electric tomorrow? ⚡
videos.description:
What if every vehicle in India turned electric overnight? It sounds perfect, but there is a big problem.

City air would get cleaner and India would use far less imported oil. But charging every vehicle would need huge amounts of electricity, much of it still from coal. There would not be enough chargers, petrol pumps would close, and the grid, the batteries and the jobs would all have to change at once.

📌 Quick facts
• Coal supplies a little over 70 percent of India's electricity (Ministry of Power; check the latest year)
• India imports about 85 percent of its crude oil
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

💬 Would you switch to an electric vehicle tomorrow? Tell us in the comments.

videos.title: What if India had no internet for 7 days? 📵
videos.description:
What if India had no internet for seven days? No WhatsApp, no UPI, no maps.

You could not book a cab or order food. Offices that depend on email and video calls would stop, schools with online classes would close, and small businesses that sell online would lose a full week of sales. Hospitals, banks and airlines also depend on networks, so a lot would slow down.

📌 Quick facts
• Everyday services like payments, maps, messaging and cloud tools all depend on the internet
A thought experiment, not a forecast.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

videos.title: What if India had TWO time zones? ⏰
videos.description:
What if India had two time zones? Right now the whole country runs on one clock, but the sun rises almost two hours earlier in the northeast than in Gujarat.

In Assam, summer mornings are bright before 5 and tea gardens already run their own "garden time", an hour ahead. Two zones could mean more daylight at work and, some studies say, lower electricity use. But train timetables, flights, banks and exams would need new rules, and a confused clock on a busy single-line track can be dangerous.

📌 Quick facts
• India is nearly 3,000 kilometres wide from east to west
• The sun rises almost two hours earlier in the northeast than in Gujarat
• Russia uses 11 time zones; China, about as wide as India, uses one
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

💬 Would two time zones help or hurt? Tell us in the comments.

videos.title: What if India never invented ZERO? 0️⃣
videos.description:
What if India never gave the world zero? Zero is just a circle, but try writing 1,000 without it.

Around 1,400 years ago Indian mathematicians like Brahmagupta wrote the rules for zero as a real number. Other cultures used a gap or a dot as a placeholder, and India turned it into something you can add, subtract and calculate with. Without it we might be stuck with Roman numerals, and algebra, modern mathematics and computers all lean on zero.

📌 Quick facts
• Brahmagupta described rules for zero as a number in 628 CE
• Other cultures used a gap or a dot only as a placeholder
• XLVII × CXXIII in Roman numerals is 47 × 123 = 5,781 today
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

💬 What do you think would be different without zero? Tell us in the comments.

videos.title: What if India's population doubled to 2.8 billion? 👥
videos.description:
What if India's population doubled to 2.8 billion people?

India already has more than 1.4 billion people. Doubling that would mean twice the rice, wheat and vegetables on the same land, plus far more water, homes, jobs and electricity. Cities would grow into each other, and roads, schools and hospitals would need to double just to keep today's standard.

📌 Quick facts
• India has about 1.4 billion people, the most of any country (UN World Population Prospects 2024)
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

videos.title: What if ALL of India spoke ONE language? 🗣️
videos.description:
What if all of India spoke just one language? India has 22 official languages, and hundreds more spoken in homes, markets and villages.

One language would make exams, courts and apps work the same everywhere, and a farmer in Assam could talk to a doctor in Kerala. But a language also carries songs, jokes, proverbs and stories, many states feel strongly about whose language it would be, and millions of people would have to relearn how to read, write and do business almost overnight.

📌 Quick facts
• India has 22 officially recognised languages
• A rupee note prints its value in 15 languages
• Hundreds more languages are spoken in homes, markets and villages
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

videos.title: What if India stopped importing oil? ⛽
videos.description:
What if India stopped buying oil from other countries? Petrol pumps would run dry within weeks.

India imports roughly 85 percent of the crude oil it uses, and almost every bus, truck, bike and car runs on it. Without imports, trucks carrying vegetables, milk and grain would slow down, factories would cut production, flights would be cancelled, and prices of everything would climb.

📌 Quick facts
• India imports roughly 85% of its crude oil (Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; recent years have been 85 to 88%)
• Buses, trucks, bikes and cars run mostly on petrol and diesel made from crude
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

💬 How would your day change without petrol? Tell us in the comments.

videos.title: What if every train in India stopped for one day? 🚆
videos.description:
What if every train in India stopped for 24 hours? Over 20 million passengers would be stranded.

That is nearly the population of Australia, every single day. Workers could not reach offices, stations would fill with stranded travellers, and students would miss exams. Then the freight: trains carry coal, grain, fertiliser and fuel, and power plants depend on coal wagons arriving on time, so supply chains would begin to stall within hours.

📌 Quick facts
• Indian Railways carries about 24 million passengers a day (Ministry of Railways; depends on the year and on whether suburban trips are counted)
• Australia has about 27 million people (ABS)
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

💬 Have you ever been stuck because of a train delay? Tell us in the comments.

videos.title: What if ISRO had NASA's budget? 🚀
videos.description:
What if ISRO had as much money as NASA? India's Mars mission cost less than some Hollywood movies.

ISRO already does so much with so little. With NASA-level funding it could build bigger rockets, send more astronauts deeper into space, and launch many more satellites for farming, weather and communication, becoming a top space power much faster.

📌 Quick facts
• Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) cost about 450 crore rupees, around 74 million US dollars
• NASA's yearly budget is about 25 billion dollars (FY2024)
• ISRO's yearly budget is about 1.6 billion dollars (about 13,000 crore rupees)
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

videos.title: What if cricket never came to India? 🏏
videos.description:
What if cricket never came to India? Would the IPL even exist?

Cricket arrived with the British and is now by far the biggest sport in the country. Without it another sport, maybe hockey, football or kabaddi, might have taken its place. Advertising money, sponsorships and TV deals would flow elsewhere, and millions of children would have idolised someone other than Tendulkar, Dhoni or Kohli.

📌 Quick facts
• Cricket arrived in India with the British in the 1700s
• India won Olympic hockey gold six times in a row from 1928 to 1956, and again in 1964 and 1980
Figures are approximate and rounded.

🎬 Follow for more "What if...?" explainers about India.

videos.title: What if UPI stopped working for one whole day? 📱
videos.description:
What if UPI stopped working for one whole day? Most of us barely carry cash anymore.

UPI handles billions of payments every month, from big shops to a chai stall on the roadside. If it went down, millions of people would reach the counter and not be able to pay, ATMs would have long queues, and bills, rent and online orders would stall. For many small businesses, one day without payments is a day without income.

📌 Quick facts
• UPI handles billions of payments every month (NPCI publishes the monthly volumes; check the latest)
Figures are approximate and rounded.
